C-HASHLINE-DENY-SAFETY.IntentSummary: Fix hashline-edit so an explicit permission denial is honored and plugin-owned tool definitions are never restored from the captured host definitions map. Delivers AC-01 through AC-07 of the approved GraceChangeSpec. Approved by explicit user instruction; execution has not started.

MustContain.Text: no genuine native definition was observed.

PlanningNotes.Note: Approval provenance: the user approved the GraceChangeSpec C-HASHLINE-DENY-SAFETY and invoked grace-plan. This plan is draft until the user approves it; no implementation has started.
Design principle is load-bearing: an explicit permission denial outranks routing. The plugin may choose among host-permitted editors, but it must never resurrect tools the host removed under a deny.

Two distinct defects: (1) the crash because plugin-owned definitions are seeded before registration and are therefore never in the captured map; (2) the capability bypass because host-native edit and write are re-added under a deny. Both are addressed by the ownership split plus the deny no-op.

Ownership split: plugin-owned tools (hashline_edit, str_replace_editor) restore from the plugin's own definitions object; host-native tools (edit, write, patch) restore from the captured host definitions map, preserving the honest refusal when a host-native tool was never captured and edit-family tools remain visible.

Deny no-op placement: the check runs after the disabled/unbound branch and only when hashline-edit is enabled; when the live session tool set exposes no edit-family tool the handler returns without mutating or throwing, honoring the host decision.

Regression trigger: the release-summary agent (permission deny-all, one step) with a project config enabling hashline-edit and routing deepseek to str_replace_editor. The release tooling itself is not changed; that interaction is out of scope.

Test-fixture correction is part of the fix: the host registry fixture must not seed plugin-owned tools, matching the real capture order, and deny-all regression tests are added for both plugin-owned modes.
No final-review obligation is declared by the source. Any reviewer the controller independently requests is optional, not a recorded gate.

GRACE lifecycle commands (grace lint, grace status, --assertions baseline/target/final) are external execution gates and must never be nested in a MustPassCommand or task verification; the pre-implementation active-baseline check is grace lint --path . --assertions current.

T-001.Title: Honor permission denial and separate tool-definition ownership in hashline-edit.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Add a helper `hasObservedEditFamily` that reports whether the live session tool set exposes any edit-family tool, and define an `OWNED_EDIT_TOOLS` set for the plugin-owned tools hashline_edit and str_replace_editor.

In sessionContext, after the disabled/unbound branch and only when hashline-edit is enabled, return without mutating or throwing when no edit-family tool is observed, honoring an explicit host denial.

Add an `ownedToolDefinitions` alias to the plugin's own tools object and use it to restore plugin-owned desired tools, while host-native desired tools continue to restore from the captured native definitions map.
Preserve the honest refusal: a host-native desired tool that was never captured and whose edit-family tools remain visible still throws the existing error rather than fabricating a definition.
Update the module contract, module map, and change summary in src/plugins/hashline-edit/index.ts to describe deny-safety and the ownership split, crediting this change.

T-002.Title: Correct the registry fixture and add deny-all regression tests.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Remove hashline_edit and str_replace_editor from the host registry fixture in src/plugins/hashline-edit.integration.test.ts so the fixture matches the real capture order where plugin-owned tools are not seeded.

Add a deny-all regression test for routing to str_replace_editor and one for routing to hashline_edit: the session tool set is empty or lacks every edit-family tool, the handler does not throw, and it adds no tools.
Add a regression test where a plugin-owned desired tool is absent from the live set but edit-family tools remain visible, proving it is restored from the plugin's own definition.

Keep the existing per-model override tests passing: GPT routed to edit restores genuine edit and write; non-GPT routed to apply_patch restores native patch; GPT routed to hashline_edit exposes hashline_edit and write and hides patch and edit.
Update the test module contract, module map, and change summary to cover deny-safety and the corrected fixture, crediting this change.

Update M-PLUGIN-HASHLINE-EDIT Purpose in .grace/graph/main.xml only where behavior changed, without altering Paths or Depends.
Run bun run check and the hashline-edit suites; no unrelated source, schema, package surface, or generated dist file is changed.
